name: Nettipattam — the Elephant Caparison
tagline: The gold-coloured face ornament worn by festival elephants
summary: Nettipattam, the ornate caparison of Kerala's festival elephants: history, craftsmanship, Thrissur Pooram and where to see and buy a replica.
description: A nettipattam is the large, gold-coloured ornament fixed over a festival elephant's forehead. It is made of copper or brass plates, with a pattern of lotus petals and bells, and finished with tassels.
Elephants wearing nettipattam, with bells at their necks and decorated tusks, lead temple processions across Kerala, most famously at Thrissur Pooram.

history.significance: A sign of temple pageantry, tying craft, ritual and the culture of the elephant in Kerala.

timeline.event: Elephants are used in temple rituals and royal processions across South India.
Elaborate caparisons are made by craft families for temple festivals.
Festival demand for nettipattam supports craft families; regulations govern the treatment of captive elephants.

keyFacts: Nettipattam are fitted by experienced handlers and mahouts; the elephant is treated as part of the temple.
Thrissur Pooram (April–May) is the most famous elephant festival, with a procession of decorated elephants.
Kerala has laws and guidelines governing the use of captive elephants in festivals.
Replica nettipattam are sold as decorative wall pieces.

folklore.title: The Elephant and the Temple
story: The elephant is regarded as a carrier of the deity at festivals. Temples say the tradition of decorating the animal is a mark of honour, with the nettipattam placed over the forehead on the morning of the procession.
Craft families recall that new designs were commissioned by temple committees and rival temple groups, which led to the competitive artistry visible at Thrissur Pooram.
folklore.note: Accounts vary by temple; consult temple committees.

spiritual.summary: For many people the sight of decorated elephants at dawn is a moving link to temple devotion.

experiences.title: Thrissur Pooram
experiences.text: Watch from a safe public area as the processions form; arrive early and respect barricades.

experiences.title: Visit the elephant sanctuary
experiences.text: Punnathur Kotta near Guruvayur houses temple elephants (verify visiting rules and animal welfare).

mindfulTips: Keep a safe distance from elephants.
Do not feed or touch the elephants.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Festival season January to May; Thrissur Pooram falls in April–May (check dates).
visitorInfo.howToReach: Thrissur is on the main rail line; the Pooram is held on the Thekkinkadu Maidan around the Vadakkunnathan Temple.
etiquette: Do not approach or touch elephants.
Follow police crowd instructions at festivals.
Do not use flash near the animals.

heritage.materials: Copper or brass plates, gold-coloured plating, bells, tassels

whereToSee.name: Thrissur Pooram, Vadakkunnathan Temple
whereToSee.note: Annual festival with processions of decorated elephants.

whereToBuy.name: Surabhi — Handicrafts Development Corporation of Kerala emporiums
whereToBuy.note: State-run emporiums selling metalcraft, wood carving, coir and handloom; good for fixed-price first purchases.

whereToBuy.name: Kairali — Kerala State Handicrafts Apex Co-operative Society emporiums
whereToBuy.note: Government-linked craft emporiums in major towns; fixed prices and craft-certified items.

whereToBuy.name: Thrissur craft shops
whereToBuy.note: Replica nettipattam are sold as decorative pieces; ask for a written bill and check craftsmanship.

experiences.name: Punnathur Kotta Elephant Sanctuary
experiences.note: Elephant sanctuary near Guruvayur; check welfare standards and visiting hours.

buyingTips: Buy replicas only; ritual caparisons are not for sale.
Check weight and plating; handmade pieces are heavy.
Ask for packing for air travel.
